edges.description: Loss of beta-enolase activity blocks the interconversion of 2-phosphoglycerate and phosphoenolpyruvate, interrupting glycolysis at the penultimate step of the distal pathway.
Impaired glycolytic ATP supply during higher-intensity exercise produces an exertional energy shortfall in glycolytic fibres.
Reduced glycolytic ATP supply limits sustained and higher-intensity exercise.
Exertional energy failure produces post-exercise muscle pain.
Exertional metabolic stress in glycolytic fibres provokes cramping.
When the energy shortfall is severe enough, sarcolemmal integrity fails and the fibre breaks down.
Myofiber breakdown with release of intracellular contents.
Myoglobin released during rhabdomyolysis is excreted, producing pigmenturia.
Myofiber membrane injury releases creatine kinase, which rises with rhabdomyolysis while typically remaining normal between episodes.

nodes.description: Biallelic ENO3 variants reduce or abolish muscle beta-enolase. Two distinct molecular routes are documented: destabilising missense substitutions that lower the amount of correctly folded dimeric enzyme, and variants that leave higher residual activity but alter the enzyme's kinetic profile. Beta-enolase accounts for over 90% of enolase activity in adult human muscle, so there is no effective isoform redundancy in that tissue.

nodes.description: Structural breakdown of the muscle fibre with release of intracellular contents. This is the structural consequence of the metabolic event above, and is separated from it because the two are dissociable in this disorder: the 2001 index patient had the metabolic phenotype without pigmenturia, whereas every patient reported since has had recurrent rhabdomyolysis. Serum creatine kinase is characteristically normal between episodes and rises only with rhabdomyolysis, distinguishing GSDXIII from the myopathic glycogenoses that carry a persistently raised CK.

nodes.description: Supportive management of rhabdomyolysis episodes, including hydration and, in severe myoglobinuric episodes, renal replacement therapy. Modality is recorded as OTHER rather than DEVICE because the treatment is the supportive-care bundle as a whole; dialysis is the most intensive element of it, not the treatment itself.
